name: hazel_weir_central_procedural_graph
description: Optimized procedural execution graph featuring dedicated workforce acceleration, high-velocity oracle peak capture, continuous town shop preemption, and strict payroll protection.

nodes.name: State & Balance Audit
nodes.description: Computes net available cash, shed fill percentage, wage liability, and oracle price drop signals.

nodes.name: Midnight Wage Reserve Defense
nodes.description: Protects payroll for all active hired hands. Blocks capital expenditure and triggers pre-midnight surplus liquidation to prevent the 0-hand bankruptcy cascade.

nodes.name: Town Shop Demand Arbitrage
nodes.description: Preemptively fulfills unlocked town shop contracts (Carrots, Tomatoes, Strawberries, Eggs) to lock in 2x-3x price premiums before open market disposal.

nodes.name: Aggressive Workforce Expansion
nodes.description: Scales workforce aggressively to the 10-hand maximum as early as possible once payroll runway is secured, maximizing farm labor velocity and harvest yields.

nodes.name: Shed Headroom Relief
nodes.description: Prevents silent 100/100 harvest discards by clearing low-margin non-feed inventory at fair prices when shed approaches true capacity.

nodes.name: Oracle Market Timing & Paced Liquidation
nodes.description: Leverages 96-step oracle forecasts and spot prices to systematically monetize harvest surpluses at cyclical price peaks and front-run predicted gluts in paced tranches.

nodes.name: High-Yield Crop & Market Synchronization
nodes.description: Directs seed budgeting and field planting toward high profit-per-hour crops (Strawberries, Tomatoes, Carrots) synchronized with shop demands, restricting wheat to livestock feed.

nodes.name: Routine Farm & Workforce Execution
nodes.description: Executes field routines (planting, watering, feeding livestock, harvesting) using available action slots.

attributes.guidance: Cancel non-essential purchases (BUY_SEED, BUY_ANIMAL, redundant HIRE); enforce emergency sales of non-feed inventory at hour >= 20 in sized tranches to meet exact payroll shortfall; schedule worker harvest drop-offs before hour 21.
attributes.pitfalls: Never sell Wheat below livestock feed reserve (n_animals * 2); do not liquidate high-multiplier town shop crops to cover minor payroll deficits if non-feed items or surplus wool/fertilizer suffice.

attributes.guidance: Fulfill town shop contract demands (Carrots, Tomatoes, Strawberries, Eggs) immediately to capture 2x-3x price premiums; prioritize shop fulfillment over all open-market sales; align seed budgeting and planting schedules to anticipated shop contract refreshes.
attributes.pitfalls: Never sell wheat needed for livestock feed buffer; do not withhold inventory waiting for future theoretical shops if current shop orders are active and unfulfilled.

attributes.condition: n_hands < 10 and net_available_cash >= hire_cost + midnight_payroll_due + (n_hands + 1) * 150.0 and day <= 22
attributes.guidance: Hire an additional hand immediately when liquid cash covers the hiring fee plus midnight payroll and a conservative next-day wage buffer; reaching the 10-hand maximum early compounds field throughput, harvest speed, and total farm revenue.
attributes.pitfalls: Do not hire if doing so reduces cash below midnight payroll requirement; do not hire past the 10-hand ceiling; do not hire late in the game (after day 22) when new hands cannot recoup their hiring fee.

attributes.guidance: Evict lowest-margin inventory (fertilizer, surplus wheat above reserve, raw wool) at market price >= 0.60 * base_price in tranches of 10-15 units; cancel stale buy orders to recover order slots; route eligible goods to town shops before generic open-market liquidation.
attributes.pitfalls: Never sell town shop contract crops or feed wheat below reserve (n_animals * 2); avoid dumping items below 0.50 * base_price; do not wait until shed reaches 95+ where simultaneous worker drop-offs trigger silent inventory loss.

attributes.condition: (oracle_glut_risk >= 0.40 and current_price >= 0.80 * base_price) or (current_price >= 1.05 * base_price and shed_used >= 8) or (day >= 28 and shed_used >= 5)
attributes.guidance: Execute sales in paced batches (10-15 units per order) to prevent order book slippage; seize cyclical price peaks above base price promptly without waiting for high shed saturation; front-run forecasted gluts by clearing non-contract inventory before price crashes; preserve livestock feed reserve and town shop commitments.
attributes.pitfalls: Never dump oversized single-turn market orders (> 20 units) that crash market prices; do not sell wheat below animal feed buffer; do not hold inventory through peak windows waiting for shed fill percentage to rise.

attributes.guidance: Direct planting capacity and seed purchases toward top profit-per-hour crops: Strawberries and Tomatoes on days 1-25; synchronize planting with active and upcoming Town Shop demands (Carrots, Tomatoes, Strawberries); transition to Tomatoes and fast-maturing Carrots on days 26-28; restrict wheat planting strictly to sustain the livestock feed buffer; preserve cash buffer for midnight payroll.
attributes.pitfalls: Do not plant Strawberries after day 25 or Tomatoes after day 27 as they will not mature before turn 720; cease all planting by day 28 hour 20 to avoid unharvested seed waste; never compromise the midnight payroll reserve.

attributes.guidance: Dispatch idle hands to harvesting ready crops, watering unwatered plots, feeding livestock, clearing weeds, and planting queued seeds in priority order; ensure workers drop off carried inventory before end of turn 717.
attributes.pitfalls: Do not leave mature crops unharvested or drying unwatered for consecutive turns; ensure workers drop all carried inventory into the shed before terminal steps (turn 718-720).
